title: The AI Lawyer

sections.body: The AI Lawyer covers how artificial intelligence is used in legal work rather than how it is imagined in courtrooms. In discovery, systems classify and rank large document sets, flag privilege, and surface patterns across email, chat, and contracts. In contracts, tools extract clauses, compare drafts against playbooks, and generate first-pass language for review. Legal research tools retrieve statutes, cases, and secondary sources, then summarize them with citations that a lawyer must check. Corporate compliance teams use AI to monitor regulatory changes, screen third parties, and test controls, while intellectual property teams use it for trademark clearance, patent landscaping, and infringement detection. Litigation teams use prediction models to estimate outcomes, value cases, and plan arguments, while operations teams use it for billing, staffing, and security monitoring.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this work are genuinely solved at a narrow level. Document review and contract extraction can reach useful accuracy on well-defined tasks, and legal research retrieval is fast and broad. The hard parts remain reasoning, privilege, confidentiality, bias, and accountability. Language models can invent citations, misread jurisdiction, and miss the fact pattern that changes the answer. Courts and regulators are still deciding how to treat AI-generated work, and the site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, plus 29 AI case law precedents. Regulation is fragmented, with 219 compliance and regulation pages and 6978 state AI bills showing how much is still unsettled, and no system replaces a lawyer's judgment or removes the need for verification.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section divide the field by legal function and by the infrastructure that supports it. E-Discovery and Large-Scale Document Analysis is the place to start for review workflows, while Contract Lifecycle and Algorithmic Drafting covers extraction, drafting, and playbook automation. Legal Research and Case Strategy explains retrieval and citation checking, and Corporate Governance and Regulatory Compliance covers board duties, controls, and monitoring. Intellectual Property and Trademark Strategy handles clearance, patents, and infringement, while Litigation Prediction and Judicial Analytics examines outcome models and their limits. Legal Operations, Infrastructure and Security covers billing, staffing, and the systems underneath, and Data Privacy and Cyber-Regulatory Compliance covers privacy and cyber rules. Emerging Legal Frameworks tracks the law being written now, and AI Security Audits and Enterprise Enablement covers the audits and controls that let firms and legal departments adopt these tools.
